title: Classic Adventure
build: Single-file disk transfer of the tape release: CLASSIC ADV. on a disk named DIGITAL DUNGEON 98, with a relocating wrapper

credits.role: Conversion of Crowther and Woods' Adventure; the inlay says (c) 1983 John Jones-Steele and the title screen (c)Abersoft 1984
Inlay artwork, as the inlay credits it

tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.5, no display (cloud container)

exclude: BASIC's CHRGET, which the BASIC ROM puts in zero page at power-on and RUN runs before the game starts (codemap.json records it); the game never calls it or uses these bytes
the KERNAL's work area and vectors: the game keeps nothing here, and wrapper_start only puts the KERNAL's own default vectors back at $031A
screen RAM: init_screen clears it with CHROUT $93 and all text goes through CHROUT, so the hand-over's screen (the boot and LOAD messages) is not the game's

left behind by the wrapper's move: $083F-$0B40 are the loaded file's bytes, each equal to the one $0340 above it, and $0B41-$0B9D the moved copy of the BASIC line and the wrapper's first half, which never runs there. No instruction reads either; the STA $0A40,X that opcodes.py --refs names is wrapper_move's operand as the loop left it after its last page, $0B40, and never ran with that value
the power-on pattern of RAM ($00 and $FF in turn) saved with the file between stale_code and the dictionary; nothing reads it
the file's last two bytes, zero, after the object table; nothing reads them (the object loops stop at object 78, $8B3D) and SAVE stops before them

RAM above the program, which the file never reaches (the move ends at $8B3F): the name CLASSIC ADV. at $9FF4 is where VICE's autostart left the file name it loaded by, and the rest is the RAM's power-on pattern; nothing reads any of it

the KERNAL ROM: $01 stays $36, so every address here the game calls or reads ($FD36, $FFBA-$FFD8, the reset vector at $FFFC) is the ROM's, and the RAM beneath holds nothing of the game, whose file ends at $8B3F
